" Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. In the event of the CO alarm sounding, follow these 3 steps: VENTILATE : Keep calm; open doors and windows to ventilate your home. Stop using fuel-burning appliances and turn them off. EVACUATE : Evacuate the property immediately. RING FOR HELP: If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. Do not use appliances until they have been checked by an expert. Get medical help for anyone suffering the effects of CO poisoning. What are the symptoms of CO poisoning? Symptoms of CO poisoning include headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea and vomiting, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, seizures, chest pain, disorientation, and loss of consciousness. Who should I call in the event of a CO leak? If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. What are the sources of CO? The common sources of Carbon Monoxide (CO) are cookers, fires, boilers, oil and gas boilers, portable generators, oil or solid fuel cookers, gas or paraffin heaters, barbecues (BBQs), clogged chimneys, wood or gas fireplaces, cigarette smoke or any fossil fuel‑burning appliances. Product description Product Description Achieve all-day flawless makeup with The UK's #1 Setting Spray*, L'Oréal Paris Infallible 36H Setting Spray mist. This ultra-fine mist extends your makeup wear, preventing transfer, smudging, and fading for up to 36 hours. Experience our fastest-drying setting spray yet, with a 3-second dry-down that leaves your skin feeling light, comfortable, and never sticky. Infallible 36H Setting Spray is your ultimate weapon against makeup meltdown. Whether you're battling humidity, rain, or sweat, this setting spray locks in your look, keeping your makeup fresh and vibrant all day and night. Say goodbye to touch-ups and hello to transfer-proof, sweat-proof, and worry-proof wear. This lightweight formula creates an invisible shield that protects your makeup from the elements, ensuring a flawless finish that lasts. Perfect for all skin types, Infallible 36H Setting Spray is a must-have for anyone who wants their makeup to stay put, no matter what. Experience the long-lasting power of Infallible and keep your makeup looking its best, from morning to night. Simply spritz over your finished makeup look and enjoy all-day confidence. I was pleasantly surprised to discover I was wrong! I haven't used any high-end setting powders to really be able to accurately compare, but it does the job. I didn't have any issues with the product arriving damaged, but I guess I was just lucky to have a courier who handles parcels with care. I have combination skin, but a rather oily t-zone. I use oil-free skincare and base makeup products, but some of the oil will still seep through. I've used other drugstore setting powders that have received high praises and reviews, but they only ever mattify my t-zone for a short duration. This powder seems to set my makeup almost immediately, and absorbs into the skin so doesn't leave any residue to dust off even when baking. It minimises the oil for quite a few hours. I have only ever worn it on night outs and not for a whole day, so I can imagine if you have very oily skin you might need to do a light touch-up or use blotting papers to remove any excess shine. My only complaint is that the translucent shade is slightly pale, so not a true universal translucent colour. Lucky for me that my foundation is a shade paler than my natural skin tone, or else I think it could be airing on the side of being too light for my medium brown skin. I fear it may leave a white cast on someone with a darker complexion... :3 Additionally, the powder is thick/full-coverage (doesn't feel heavy when worn though). Because of my combination skin type, I can get away with matte makeup products without it making my complexion look dry or dull as there will always be a small amount of dewiness coming through. However, for someone with dry or normal skin I can imagine this becoming cakey quite easily. Therefore, would only really recommend as a powder for those with oily or combination skin. Overall, it's a decent powder for the price paid. Of course it's not going to compare to cult favourites like Charlotte Tilbury's, but it's a great budget alternative :) More Hide Thank you for your feedback Close Sorry, there was an error Close Sorry, we couldn't load the review Try again Filtering customer reviews Loading customer reviews There was a problem filtering reviews. This was my first time trying CeraVe Foaming Cleanser, and I have been using it consistently for about a month. Overall: I think this is a good everyday facial cleanser and the large bottle gives decent value over time. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. Dopo aver provato praticamente tutti i detergenti CeraVe, posso dire che questa è la versione che preferisco in assoluto per la mia pelle. Ho una pelle mista, quindi con alcune zone che tendono a lucidarsi e diventare più oleose e altre che invece possono risultare più secche. Per questo ho sempre cercato un detergente che riuscisse a pulire bene senza lasciarmi quella sensazione di pelle "tirata" dopo il lavaggio. Nel corso del tempo ho provato praticamente tutte le versioni della linea CeraVe. Ho iniziato anche dall'olio detergente, proprio perché cercavo qualcosa di estremamente delicato. Mi è piaciuto, soprattutto per la sensazione che lasciava e per la profumazione, ma personalmente non era quello con cui mi trovavo meglio. Ho poi provato la crema detergente e, invece, non sono riuscito ad apprezzarla particolarmente. Soprattutto in estate, la sensazione durante l'utilizzo mi risultava troppo simile a quella di spalmare una crema sul viso e non era la tipologia di detersione che cercavo. Con la Schiuma Detergente, invece, ho trovato finalmente il compromesso che cercavo. LA SCHIUMA FA DAVVERO LA DIFFERENZA La prima cosa che si nota è ovviamente la consistenza: a contatto con l'acqua il detergente produce una bella schiuma. Ora, dal punto di vista scientifico, più schiuma non significa necessariamente più pulizia. È un aspetto importante perché spesso associamo inconsciamente una grande quantità di schiuma a un prodotto più efficace. Però c'è anche un aspetto più pratico e personale: a me la schiuma piace. Durante la skincare trovo molto più piacevole massaggiare una schiuma sul viso rispetto a una crema o a un olio. È una piccola cosa, ma secondo me il fatto che una routine sia piacevole da fare aumenta anche la probabilità di riuscire a mantenerla con costanza. La skincare, alla fine, non è soltanto una questione di ingredienti: anche la sensorialità del prodotto conta nell'esperienza quotidiana. PERCHÉ È ADATTA ALLA PELLE MISTA La formula è pensata per detergere rimuovendo sebo, impurità e residui senza compromettere eccessivamente la barriera cutanea. CeraVe utilizza in questa linea ceramidi e acido ialuronico, ingredienti interessanti soprattutto perché la detersione non dovrebbe limitarsi a "sgrassare" la pelle, ma dovrebbe cercare di mantenere un buon equilibrio tra pulizia e comfort. Le ceramidi, in particolare, sono lipidi naturalmente presenti nella barriera cutanea e svolgono un ruolo importante nel mantenimento della funzione barriera. È quindi sensato trovarle all'interno di una linea cosmetica che punta a detergere senza lasciare la pelle inutilmente impoverita. Il detergente contiene inoltre niacinamide, ingrediente molto versatile che viene utilizzato frequentemente nelle formulazioni destinate alle pelli miste o impure. Una cosa che apprezzo è proprio il fatto che, dopo il risciacquo, non mi rimane quella sensazione di "pelle che tira" che personalmente associo a una detersione troppo aggressiva. COME LO UTILIZZO Ne basta davvero poco. Inumidisco il viso, erogo una piccola quantità di prodotto e lo massaggio delicatamente sulla pelle, senza sfregare eccessivamente. Poi risciacquo con acqua. Non vedo la necessità di utilizzare una quantità enorme di detergente: la schiuma si distribuisce bene e una confezione da 473 ml dura davvero a lungo. Ed è proprio questo uno dei motivi per cui considero questo formato particolarmente conveniente. 473 ML: UN FORMATO CHE FA LA DIFFERENZA Questa secondo me è una delle caratteristiche più sottovalutate. Molti detergenti che mi incuriosiscono, soprattutto alcuni prodotti coreani, vengono venduti in confezioni da 150, 200 o 250 ml. Non è necessariamente un problema, ma quando si utilizza un detergente ogni giorno, mattina e/o sera, il prodotto finisce abbastanza rapidamente. Qui invece abbiamo 473 ml, quindi quasi mezzo litro. Considerando che ne basta poco ad ogni utilizzo, una confezione mi dura veramente parecchio. Per una skincare quotidiana è un vantaggio enorme, soprattutto se si vuole evitare di ricomprare continuamente il detergente. LA MIA ESPERIENZA Dopo aver provato praticamente tutta la gamma detergente CeraVe, questa è quella che ricomprerei più volentieri. Non perché sia necessariamente "la migliore" per qualsiasi tipo di pelle, ma perché è quella che si adatta meglio alle mie esigenze. La mia pelle mista ha bisogno di una detersione che mi faccia sentire il viso pulito senza trasformare il lavaggio in un momento in cui la pelle viene aggredita. La schiuma rende inoltre l'utilizzo molto piacevole e il formato da 473 ml permette di utilizzarlo quotidianamente senza preoccuparsi troppo dei consumi. PRO: ✅ Ottimo compromesso per pelle mista. ✅ Schiuma piacevole e facile da distribuire. ✅ Non lascia, nel mio caso, una sensazione eccessiva di pelle che tira. ✅ Formula con ceramidi, acido ialuronico e niacinamide. ✅ 473 ml: formato molto più conveniente rispetto a molti detergenti più piccoli. ✅ Ne basta poco e quindi dura davvero tanto. CONTRO: ❌ Se non amate i detergenti schiumogeni, probabilmente questa non è la consistenza che state cercando. ❌ La schiuma è piacevole ma non significa automaticamente che il prodotto deterge più di un detergente che fa poca schiuma. VALUTAZIONE FINALE Dopo aver provato praticamente tutti i detergenti CeraVe, questa è la versione che sceglierei nuovamente. Per la mia pelle mista trovo che sia il compromesso migliore tra sensazione di pulizia, comfort e piacevolezza durante l'utilizzo. Non mi lascia quella sensazione eccessivamente sgrassata che personalmente non amo, ma allo stesso tempo mi dà la sensazione di aver lavato bene il viso. Il vero punto forte, però, è l'insieme: buona sensorialità, formula pensata per rispettare la barriera cutanea, poca quantità necessaria e un formato enorme da 473 ml. Non sarà il detergente più "instagrammabile" o quello con la confezione più particolare, ma dopo averne provati così tanti, alla fine mi sono reso conto che quello che cerco nella skincare quotidiana è proprio questo: un prodotto che funziona, che mi piace utilizzare e che non devo ricomprare ogni due settimane. " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Reliable, long-lasting power for variety of devices - wipe off the bitter coating or sticker residue I bought this Duracell lithium 4-pack specifically to replace the dead factory coin cells in my daily-use blood glucometer and our digital bathroom weighing scales, and am very happy with this purchase. Performance Breakdown: Build Quality & Safety: The physical construction of these batteries is excellent. A standout feature is the bitter-tasting ring coating on the back, which provides great peace of mind if you have small children or pets in the house. There is a little black sticker at the back of each battery. It is designed to alert parents to the extreme choking and internal burn hazard these batteries pose to infants and toddlers. You must peel it off: The sticker is made of non-conductive plastic. If you leave the sticker on when you put the battery into your device, it will completely block the electric current, as will the bitter coating if a device's internal terminal tabs happen to line up exactly where that clear, non-conductive bitter coating is placed; the device won't get any electricity and will not turn on. If this happens (as it did to me), you will need to scrub the battery clean with isopropyl alcohol to get a reliable electrical connection. Quick solution that works. The child-secure plastic packaging is exceptionally tough—you will definitely need a good pair of scissors to get them out. Real-World Power: Once installed, both devices powered up instantly with full battery indicators. My glucometer screen is noticeably crisper, and the Bluetooth syncing to my phone has been flawless. Unlike cheap generic brands that cause scales to throw intermittent "Low Batt" errors after a week, these have provided steady, uninterrupted voltage. Longevity: Having used Duracell coin cells in the past, they easily last 12+ months in low-drain devices. The 10-year shelf life is brilliant. There are many options on Amazon that claim years long shelf life, but have no specified manfacture date, without which, one can't tell how long the batteries have actually been sitting on a shelf. Duracel is very transparent and clearly shows the manufacture and expiration dates at the back of the packaging. Limitations: The Bitterant Coating Catch: As already mentioned, the child-safety bitterant coating can occasionally cause a connection issue in very specific devices. If your scale or glucometer has deeply recessed or flush terminal tabs, the coating can act as a minor insulator. so if your device doesn’t turn on immediately, again, simply wipe the back of the battery firmly with an alcohol prep pad to clear the residue, and it works perfectly. Except for this, I really cannot think of any other issue that needs to be pointed out. Final Verdict: this is a versatile, good quality product from a trusted brand and a premium, reliable choice for variety of electronic devices. The 4 pack at AROUND £ 5 is a good value for money. Definitely recommended.
